items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1958-08-08; 1958-09-03
items.q: We had, she had numbers that we played for her to dance by, you know.

ctx.x: Well I was going to ask one more question about that first band on that show, you know, with Mamie Lane and all. What kind of music did you play? Did you just play for her singing or did you play other pieces too?

Yeah, we had a regular routine, yeah. We had, she had numbers that we played for her to dance by, you know. And we used to play roles, not rolling, we used to play on the Rowdy League. Oh yeah, Rowdy League. Yeah, we played that, she used to dance that. Then we had a couple of band numbers we done, you see.
Some of the New Orleans numbers?

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: I come right behind Manuel Perez and them, and went with this girl, Mabel Elaine.

ctx.x: No. Mabel Elaine and her jazz band. She's a white girl. She used to clunk band. You know how Boa Jingles used to dance with wooden shoes on. She had the same thing. She used to be in a bale of cotton. She was blackface. When you get on the stage, that bale of cotton was out there. They couldn't go out. We'd be all lying around in this cotton, see, with a couple of holes on, satin cover holes, different colors, and bandana, hangers, and hats. So I had, when we started playing, this fave of cotton opened up. And…
